correctness.rationale: For p=1 every Fourier coefficient is the product of a(1-(-1)^n exp(-a*pi))/(pi(a²+n²)), strictly positive; finite atomic Fourier uniqueness proves strictness. For each finite p>1, R_t bounded by one and R_tt nonnegative with integral at most one, so the scalar marginal F has absolutely continuous first derivative and integrable F second derivative; F′(0)=0, F′(pi)<0. Exact twice integrated axial Fourier identity and Riemann-Lebesgue yield a negative limit for n² times even axial coefficients. A negative compact-group Fourier coefficient gives a genuine finite-matrix witness, with higher dimensions inherited by restriction. No finite experiment substitutes for proof. Exact constants and normalizations were independently reconstructed and script rerun on actual local path.

value.rationale: The parameter p is the canonical interpolation between additive and Euclidean intrinsic product-circle norms used for covariance modeling. The classification gives a sharp discontinuity at p=1 for every bandwidth and every number of circle factors at least two, resolves whether finite-p anisotropic geodesic Laplace covariance matrices are universally valid, and computes a forced high-frequency negative axial coefficient with explicit dependence on p and a. That tail explains why fixed-resolution grids may incorrectly suggest validity near the endpoint. This is a natural full family classification rather than a finite isolated invariant or a numerical exercise.
